title: Test Code DRYed to Loss of Completeness
pattern: Hiding test setup and state initialization details inside generic shared helper functions solely to eliminate textual duplication.
why_bad: It erodes test completeness. A reader must jump out of the test body to understand the context. Changing a "default helper" setting to fix one test can break dozens of other tests silently.
detection: Test cases that do not configure their own essential test state locally, relying entirely on shared, parameter-less setup helpers, and asserting on specific fields.
counterexample: Infrastructure mocks (e.g., database connection setups) where individual test data state is not the focus.
source: *Software Engineering at Google*, Chapter 12: "Unit Testing" — "DAMP, Not DRY", p. 248-250.
